extracted.intended_audience: individual investors (members of the public who may wish to submit comments on SEC rulemakings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for individual investors on how to prepare and submit written comments in SEC rulemaking proceedings, including what to include, how to support positions, and how to submit comments. Focuses on making comments useful to staff and ensuring submitters understand posting/privacy policies and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any comment has value
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comment, including a simple statement of whether you support or oppose a proposal or parts of a proposal, has value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the more you are able to share about your personal experience and the reasons for your views, the more useful it is for staff and the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand what you are commenting on
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you write your comment, consider taking time to read the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals, you can also find a short summary posted by the SEC online. In addition, there may be other materials available that help provide information about the rulemaking, such as a Fact Sheet, Press Release, and/or speech or statement by a Commissioner. (Background: concept releases outline topics and questions; proposing releases contain text of proposed rule, purpose discussion, and economic analysis; adopting releases contain the final rule and explanation of how the SEC arrived at it.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe relevant information about yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: Include relevant information about yourself that helps explain your perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could include the fact that you are an individual investor, how many years you have been investing, or any relevant experience you have had as an investor. Consider explaining how the rulemaking would affect you, an individual investor. You may submit your comment anonymously, and you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the section/issue, state your opinion, and explain why
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly identify the section, issue, or question you are discussing; indicate your views and explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is helpful to clearly identify the section, issue, or question you are discussing. Indicate your views and explain why. Consider discussing both what you oppose and what you support in the rulemaking. If you can, use specific examples to illustrate your views, such as your experience with an SEC rule or how the proposal would affect you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest solutions or alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If you oppose or want changes to parts of the rulemaking, propose practical solutions or alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider suggesting solutions or alternatives to the parts of the rulemaking that you oppose or think should be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide factual support and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Include factual information that supports or contradicts the rulemaking or supports your suggested solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of factual information include data or scientific evidence. Providing factual support makes comments more useful to staff and the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanics and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the procedural instructions for submitting comments and observe deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC rulemaking releases are published in the Federal Register and on SEC.gov and can be located through the SEC's Rulemaking Activity page. The online form to submit comments is accessed by the 'Submit a Comment' button for each listed rulemaking. The relevant release will contain instructions for how to submit comments, including a link to the online comment form, and the deadline for doing so. For some rulemakings, the page may also contain a link to a Feedback Flyer (a set of questions designed for individual investors). Detailed instructions on how to submit comments can also be found at 'How to Submit Comments to the SEC.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting, privacy, duplicates, and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments will be made available to the public and certain content rules and posting behaviors apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments will be made available to the public. Comments sent via online form or e-mail will be posted on the SEC's website. Comments sent via paper will be converted to PDF and then posted on the SEC's website. Do not include personal identifying information in submissions; submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. The SEC may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. Important: Please remember that the SEC does not edit personal identifying information from a submission, so submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. When multiple comments are submitted with identical or near-identical content, only the first copy of the comment received will be posted publicly, along with a running total number of that comment received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Feedback Flyers
rubrics_metrics.description: Some rulemakings provide Feedback Flyers — targeted question sets for individual investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some rulemakings, the rulemaking page may contain a link to a Feedback Flyer. A Feedback Flyer is a set of questions designed specifically for individual investors and can help structure your input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission handling
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, comments are posted and considered by the SEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After you submit a comment, it will be posted at the 'View Received Comments' link for the rulemaking on the SEC's website. The SEC considers comments received in connection with its next steps.
